title: Tabs as Steps
eyebrow: Proposal · part 3 · builds on parts 1 and 2 · nothing built yet
approval: Design approved: friction plan part 3, tabs as steps

short.lead: Today the app's screens are Focus, Sort, Board and Projects, and parts 1 and 2 added Start here, Tidy up, Triage and Roadmap. You said the tabs should each name a part of the process, and that Projects and Board don't fit. This plan has five tabs, one per step, in the order you use them: Capture, Plan, Start, Focus and Review. Nothing is dropped. Projects becomes the Roadmap, which already showed projects. The Board's three columns split across Plan, Focus and Review, so no list appears twice. Everything else from parts 1 and 2 stays as you approved it.
short.hint: Tap each row to see its picture. Start with 'The five steps', then the table at the end, which shows where every feature of Projects and Board goes.
items: One tab per step, each with one question

Capture asks what's on your mind. Plan asks what still matters and in what order. Start asks what to do now. Focus asks what you're doing. Review asks whether it's really done. Under each tab are today's screens that move into it. Settings sits outside the tabs: the gear at the top on a phone, and the bottom of the side menu on desktop.
Read the five questions left to right.

items.alt: Five cards: 1 Capture with Jotter and Sort; 2 Plan with Tidy up, Triage, Roadmap, Projects and Board Up next; 3 Start with Start here; 4 Focus with Focus and Board In progress; 5 Review with Board Done and the Needs review label

items: The jotter sits at the top. Below it are the thoughts to sort, one at a time, with the project search and the priority buttons from part 2. The bottom tabs are numbered 1 to 5, and Capture and Review show how many are waiting.
Check that Sort feels at home under Capture.

items.alt: Phone drawing: Capture tab with the jotter, 44 thoughts to sort, one thought, a project search, priority buttons, File to Chores and Later, and five numbered tabs with badges 44 and 15

items: Picking Project in the All / Area / Project switch turns the Roadmap into the project's own page. It lists every task in its Now, Next and Later blocks, with an add row, tick boxes and a status chip on each task. 'Edit project', 'Sync now' and '+ New project' move here from the Projects screen. On desktop the side menu lists the five steps, with Plan's three sub-steps under it.
Look for anything you use on the Projects screen that is missing here.

items.alt: Desktop drawing: side menu with five numbered steps and Plan's Tidy up, Triage and Roadmap; the Focus Deck project page with Sync now, Edit project, New project, and task lists in Now and Next blocks
items.caption: A project's page inside Plan, on desktop. A drawing, not built.

items: What you're doing, above what to pick next

A 'Doing now' row at the top holds every task in progress, which was the Board's middle column. The carousels (scrolling rows of cards) sit underneath, as in part 2. Each task has a small status label. Tapping the label opens a menu with Up next, Doing, Waiting for review and Done, and each one says which tab the task moves to. That menu replaces dragging cards between Board columns.
Check that the status menu is clear enough without the Board.

items.alt: Desktop drawing: Doing now row with three tasks, an open status menu with Up next, Doing, Waiting for review and Done, and the project carousel below
items.caption: Focus with the in-progress tasks on top. A drawing, not built.

items: 'Waiting for your review' lists the 15 built issues, each with 'Looks good · Done' or 'Needs more work'. 'Needs more work' sends the task back to Focus as Doing. 'Done this week' lists what you finished, with Undo. This was the Board's last column.
Read 'Looks good · Done' and 'Needs more work', and say if either is unclear.

items.alt: Phone drawing: Review tab with Waiting for your review, two issues with Looks good Done and Needs more work buttons, and Done this week with Undo
items.caption: Review on a phone. A drawing, not built.

items: Nothing from Projects or Board is lost

The table lists each thing the Projects and Board screens do today, and where it goes. 'Same' means it works as today in a new place, 'Moved' means it's reached a different way, and 'Merged' means two copies become one. Task details, with subtasks, links and labels, still open from any card.
Look for anything you use that isn't in the table.

items.alt: Table of 13 rows mapping each Projects, Board, Sort and Task details feature to its new place, marked Same, Moved or Merged
items.caption: Where each feature of today's screens goes.

changes: Five tabs: Capture, Plan, Start, Focus, Review
Numbered, in the order you use them, on phone and desktop.
The All / Area / Project switch from part 2 sits at the top of each.
Becomes Plan › Roadmap with the switch on All, Area or Project.
Add, edit, GitHub link and Sync come with it.
Its columns split: Up next to Triage, In progress to Focus, Done to Review.
A status menu on each card replaces dragging between columns.
The sorting steps stay the same.
Waiting for review, and what you finished.
'Needs more work' sends a task back to Focus.
Task details, your data and sync
choices: review
Should 'Waiting for review' become a real task status?
Yes, a fourth status
Tasks go Up next, Doing, Waiting for review, Done. On GitHub it sets and reads your Needs review label.
No, keep it as a label
Review reads the label only, and manual tasks can't be marked as waiting.
I suggest Yes, because then a task you added in the app can wait for review too, not only a GitHub issue.
board
Should the Board stay as an optional layout?
No, remove it
Its three columns live in Plan, Focus and Review, so nothing is shown twice.
Yes, as a Settings option
You can switch the old three-column view back on, but the same tasks appear in two places.
I suggest removing it, because you asked for no views that repeat each other.
startfocus
Should Start and Focus stay as two tabs?
Yes, two tabs
Start picks for you; Focus is where you choose yourself and see what you're doing.
Merge them into one 'Do' tab
Four tabs instead of five, with Start here at the top of Focus.
I suggest two tabs, because you asked for Start here not to replace Focus.

wrapup.summary: Five tabs named after the steps you take: Capture, Plan, Start, Focus and Review. Projects becomes the Roadmap, and the Board's columns split across Plan, Focus and Review, so no view repeats another.
wrapup.changing: Changed: the tabs, Projects, Board and where Sort lives. Added: the Review tab and a status menu on each card. Kept: task details, your data and sync.
wrapup.blocking: Waiting on your answers to the three questions in Choices here, and to the questions on the part 2 page. Nothing is built until you approve.
wrapup.next: After you answer, I will fold parts 1, 2 and 3 into one build order and open GitHub issues for each part.
